module_title: Reform Movements - Muslim, Parsi Reforms, and Women's Empowerment
introduction: At this level, we study the spread of education in the Muslim community (Aligarh Movement), Parsi reforms, the radical Young Bengal Movement, and the legal and social campaigns launched for the empowerment of women, especially widows.

core_concepts.title: Aligarh Movement
core_concepts.description: Initiated by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. Its goal was to connect the Muslim community with modern English education and a scientific outlook. He founded the 'Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College' (which later became Aligarh Muslim University - AMU).

core_concepts.title: Young Bengal Movement
core_concepts.description: Started in the 1820s by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio (an Anglo-Indian teacher). Inspired by the French Revolution, it was a radical movement that rejected all old traditions and customs.

core_concepts.title: Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (1856)
core_concepts.description: Due to the tireless efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, this act was drafted under Lord Dalhousie and officially passed during the tenure of Lord Canning.

core_concepts.title: Prarthana Samaj (1867)
core_concepts.description: Founded in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang and later joined by M.G. Ranade. It emphasized the teachings of the Bhakti cult and opposed the caste system and child marriage.

core_concepts.title: Theosophical Society (1875)
core_concepts.description: Founded in New York by Madam Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott (headquarters later moved to Adyar, Madras). Annie Besant popularized it in India. It focused on the revival of ancient Hindu philosophy (Upanishads).

important_entities.name: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
important_entities.significance: A great scholar from Bengal who opened around 35 schools for girls to promote women's education.

important_entities.name: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan
important_entities.significance: He advised Muslims to stay away from Congress politics and focus entirely on acquiring modern education.

important_entities.name: Annie Besant
important_entities.significance: She founded the Central Hindu College in Benares, which was later developed into the 'Banaras Hindu University' (BHU) by Madan Mohan Malaviya.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the two. The Aligarh Movement was 'Reformist' (supporting Western education), while the Deoband Movement was 'Revivalist' (an orthodox movement emphasizing pure Quranic teachings).
The abolition of Sati (1829) is associated with Raja Rammohan Roy, whereas the legal recognition of Widow Remarriage (1856) is associated with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The students of Henry Derozio were known as 'Derozians', and they are often considered the first nationalist poets of modern India.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the journals with their reformist authors: Mirat-ul-Akbar (Rammohan Roy), Gulamgiri (Jyotiba Phule), Tahdib-ul-Akhlaq (Sir Syed).
Where was the international headquarters of the Theosophical Society located? (Answer: Adyar, Madras) - This is a frequently asked question.
